decisions.reason: As the modular successor to a proven trommel screen with an already accepted market base, it likely has low carrying costs and strong continuing option value, so withdrawal within a year is unlikely.

This mobile flail shredder line sits squarely in the firm's core mobile processing business, and after several years on the market management would normally keep refining and selling it rather than exit quickly.

The mobile high-speed grinder was initially less visibly established, but if it remains in the portfolio by 2022 it has likely shown enough demand to justify keeping the option open despite some residual uncertainty.

The stationary electric fine shredder is the most niche and potentially slower-selling offer here, yet it matches the firm's resource-saving technical direction, so management would more likely retain it than abandon it immediately.

A full stationary pre-shredder line with dedicated presentation fits the firm's broader waste-processing systems portfolio well, making near-term withdrawal improbable once it has stayed in the market this long.
